Cross-Border Transmission Regimes: ANOVA and Cluster Analysis

Statistical validation of the transmission-regime taxonomy in the LEEDS MRIO-SFC model

Author

Oriol Vallès Codina

Published

October 2, 2026

0.0.1 Excluded-construction render

This is a second render of qmd/cross_border_analysis.qmd, on 12 scenarios: the two Construction scenarios — Sc5 Cnst-FD and Sc14 Cnst-Int — are withheld from sc_meta, the scenario registry, and every chunk downstream of it filters with it. The numbers, tables and dendrograms below are computed on those 12 and on nothing else.

Why they are withheld. They are the two largest divergences in the scenario set, by roughly an order of magnitude, and they are also the only two scenarios the four- and five-regime taxonomies disagree about. Both properties matter. Left in, they set the scale on which the remaining twelve are merged, so the twelve are assigned under the influence of two points that belong to no group of their own; and the partition that results can then be read as evidence about the regime count when it is mostly evidence about the two outliers.

The exclusion is the point, not a robustness check. Withholding them is the settled resolution of the four-versus-five question (audit Correction 5; ai_context/04_OPEN_QUESTIONS.md error 3). Held out, the two candidate taxonomies are the same partition on the twelve: identical(regime4, regime5) is TRUE in this render. The whole of the disagreement between them is carried by the two scenarios that are no longer here. What is left to ask of the data is whether it supports the four-group partition they agree on, and §“The exclusion, and what it changes” answers that by running both specifications side by side.

The all-fourteen counterpart of this document is output/html/cross_border_analysis.html; the two differ in nothing but the registry.

1 Introduction

This report validates the transmission-regime taxonomy used in the LEEDS MRIO-SFC model analysis of circular economy (CE) transition scenarios, on the twelve scenarios that remain once the two Construction scenarios are withheld. The scenarios it classifies into groups are these:

Regime Scenarios Mechanism
Production Leakage Sc1, 4, 9 Secondary sector’s higher import content unintentionally raises RoW intermediate exports
Symmetric Contraction Sc3, 6, 7, 8, 11, 12 Both regions contract proportionally; EU restructuring generates no directional asymmetry
Competitive Displacement Sc10 Secondary metals’ lower A-matrix row-sum frees EU intermediate resources; only scenario with true sign reversal (EU↑, RoW↓)
Fossil Import Collapse Sc2, 13 EU fossil import reduction collapses RoW hydrocarbon export revenues; RoW fiscal space deteriorates

The analysis proceeds in four stages. First, the long-term (t+20) percentage deviation from baseline is computed for each region separately, for an extended set of 34 documented aggregates across all 12 scenarios; the EU−RoW divergence Z1 − Z2 is formed from these, and the joint (Z1, Z2) profile is retained alongside it. Second, a one-way ANOVA tests whether mean divergences differ significantly across regimes for each variable, measuring the effect size with η². Third, hierarchical clustering (Ward’s D2 linkage, Euclidean distance on standardised profiles) is run in both coordinate spaces, and the presence of cluster structure is tested against a permutation null rather than against the gap statistic or a Gaussian mixture model, both of which are unidentified at p/n ≈ 2.4. Fourth, because the number of clusters is not identified at n=12, the four-group partition on which the paper’s five-regime taxonomy and CLAUDE.md’s four-regime hypothesis agree is treated as a hypothesis specified in advance and scored against the data with the adjusted Rand index, block by block, to establish which variables carry the regime signal.

3 EU−RoW Divergence Heatmap

Discussion. The heatmap reveals an immediately striking structural feature: the vast majority of cells are near-zero (white), with intense coloration concentrated in only one regime block — Fossil Import Collapse. This reflects the fundamental asymmetry of the scenario set: most CE interventions operate within small-scale material substitutions that generate proportional bilateral adjustments, while the energy transition operates through a qualitatively different channel.

Why energy (Sc2, Sc13) is so intense. The Fossil Import Collapse regime generates the deepest red cells in the ecological columns — emissions (−1.53, Sc13) — indicating that RoW’s ecological footprint deteriorates far more than EU’s in the carbon dimension. The land and water divergences for Sc13 are an order of magnitude smaller (+0.17 and −0.03 respectively): the fossil-import channel is an emissions channel, not a land or water one. The mechanism is the import substitution channel: EU households and firms reducing fossil fuel purchases shift spending toward domestically-produced renewables, concentrating the ecological gains within the EU production system. RoW energy exporters lose export revenues but do not access the domestic ecological efficiency gains that accompany the EU transition. The fiscal dimension is equally extreme: RoW government deficit diverges by −1.31 percentage points (Sc13), because hydrocarbon-exporting governments face revenue collapse. This is a canonical ecologically unequal exchange (EUE) outcome: the core economy (EU) decarbonises at the periphery’s (RoW) fiscal expense.

Why no blue block survives. The blue cells that the all-fourteen render concentrates in Construction Rebound (emissions divergences of +5.14 and +2.16) are those two scenarios’ own numbers and are not shown here, since both are withheld. Nothing on the twelve replicates them: every row in this heatmap is either near-white or red, which is the visual form of the statement that the ecological rebound in the construction scenarios has no analogue elsewhere in the scenario set. What the ecological columns do carry on the twelve is examined in “Which Variables Carry the Regime Signal?” — the short answer being very little.

Production Leakage (Sc1, Sc4, Sc9) shows moderate but consistent red in ecological columns, indicating that EU’s ecological gains exceed RoW’s — but less dramatically than the fossil scenarios. The leakage occurs through intermediate import channels: secondary-sector production in the EU draws more on RoW inputs, partially diffusing the ecological gain outward.

Competitive Displacement (Sc10) stands out uniquely in the macro columns: blue cells for consumption, value added, gross output, and employment indicate that EU outperforms RoW on macroeconomic outcomes. This is the only scenario where a true sign reversal occurs — EU macro variables move positively while RoW contracts — rather than both contracting at different rates. The intensity is moderate, however, making Sc10’s statistical distinctiveness from the Fossil Import Collapse group an open question addressed in Section 5.

4 ANOVA: Are Regime Divergences Statistically Different?

One-way ANOVA tests whether mean EU−RoW divergence differs across the 4 transmission regimes (H₀: all group means equal; df_between = 3, df_within = 8). Effect size η² = SS_between / SS_total is analogous to R². The OLS regression fits Z2 ~ Z1 across the 12 scenarios per variable, where slope > 0 indicates co-movement and slope < 0 indicates asymmetric sign reversal. Both analyses use long-term (t+20 periods) percentage deviations from baseline.

Discussion. Regime membership is a strong predictor of EU−RoW divergence: 29 of 34 variables achieve η² ≥ 0.70. Ecological and fiscal variables lead: material use (mat, η² ≈ 0.98), recycling (rec, η² ≈ 0.97), government bonds (b_s, η² ≈ 0.95), and land/emissions (η² ≈ 0.92–0.94). These are driven by the extreme divergences in the Fossil Import Collapse group.

The OLS slope column reveals the direction of bilateral co-movement. Slopes are negative for consumption, value added, employment, and wealth: as EU contracts, RoW expands (asymmetric). Slopes are strongly positive and near 1.0 for fiscal variables (government deficit, bonds): both regions’ fiscal positions move together, amplified. Ecological variables show positive slopes below 1.0, meaning RoW ecological changes are systematically smaller than EU’s in absolute terms — the ecological gains from CE accrue disproportionately to the EU production system.

Variables with low η² and near-zero slopes — wage share (shw), household loans (lh) — are regime-blind: cross-border transmission in CE scenarios does not systematically affect household financial conditions in RoW, regardless of which regime is operating.

5 Hierarchical Clustering: Two Coordinate Spaces

5.1 Why the coordinate space matters

The five transmission regimes are defined by a pair of regional signs. “Competitive Displacement” is the case where the EU expands while the Rest of World contracts; “Symmetric Contraction” is the case where both move the same way. Those are statements about the joint pattern of Z1 and Z2, not about their difference.

This has a direct consequence for how the scenarios may be clustered. A divergence of +0.5 is produced equally by (Z1 +0.4, Z2 −0.1) — a genuine sign reversal — and by (Z1 +0.6, Z2 +0.1), where both regions expand. Those are two different regimes with identical coordinates. Differencing removes the information the regime taxonomy is defined by, and no clustering algorithm can recover a distinction the coordinate transform has already destroyed.

Two spaces are therefore used throughout what follows, and they answer different questions:

space vector per scenario what it can test
Divergence Z1 − Z2 one value per variable cross-border asymmetry — how unequally a shock lands
Joint (Z1, Z2) two values per variable, standardised separately the full two-region signature, including sign patterns

The divergence space additionally destroys the current account and trade balance outright: cab and tb are bilateral accounting identities that cancel exactly between the regions, so their divergence is identically zero and they are dropped. In the joint space both survive.

5.2 Clustering Procedure

Scenarios are clustered on the 37 documented aggregates, in both spaces: 72 columns in the joint space and 34 in the divergence space. The difference is the three variables whose divergence has zero variance and is therefore dropped — cab and tb, which cancel bilaterally as accounting identities, and g, which is exogenous and identical across scenarios. All three carry information in the joint space and are retained there. Variables are standardised before clustering so that high-variance fiscal variables do not dominate the distance metric.

Algorithm: Ward’s D2 linkage with Euclidean distance. Ward’s method minimises within-cluster total variance at each merge step, producing compact, similarly-sized clusters appropriate for the small sample (n=12).

5.3 Dendrogram

Discussion. With the construction pair withheld the hierarchy has no dominant outlier, and the splits come out in the order the taxonomy predicts:

  1. First split (height 20.281 in the divergence space) separates the core nine — Sc1, Sc3, Sc4, Sc6, Sc7, Sc8, Sc9, Sc11, Sc12 — from the three high-leverage scenarios Sc2, Sc10 and Sc13. On the fourteen this first split isolates Sc5 alone; that the same split now separates a group of three is the clearest single effect of the exclusion.

  2. Second split (height 11.159) separates inside the core: {Sc1, Sc4, Sc9} from {Sc3, Sc6, Sc7, Sc8, Sc11, Sc12}. Those are Production Leakage and Symmetric Contraction, the taxonomy’s two largest regimes, recovered as the two branches.

  3. Third split (height 9.931) produces k=4 by separating {Sc2, Sc13} from {Sc10} — Fossil Import Collapse and Competitive Displacement. The k=4 cut is therefore exactly the four-regime partition, in this space and in the joint space alike.

Sc10 (Competitive Displacement) remains the weakest element. It is a singleton at k=4 and stays so at k=5 and k=6, rather than merging into the Fossil group as it does on the fourteen. Its membership is nonetheless the one the four-group taxonomy asserts, and the k=4 partition matches that taxonomy exactly — so the honest reading is that the twelve place Sc10 on its own, which is what the taxonomy claims but is a claim from a single scenario. This is taken up in “On ‘Competitive Displacement’ as a Standalone Regime” below.

5.4 How Many Clusters? Silhouette Against a Permutation Null

Three of the four criteria previously reported here — the gap statistic and the AIC and BIC of a Gaussian mixture model — are not usable on this data, and the reason is structural rather than incidental. With 34 variables and 12 scenarios, p/n ≈ 2.8.

  • The gap statistic compares observed within-cluster dispersion against a uniform reference distribution over the bounding box of the data. In 34 dimensions containing 12 points that reference is dispersed almost everywhere, the comparison degenerates, and the 1-SE rule fires at the first k it tests.
  • Gaussian mixture models estimate a mean vector and a covariance structure per component. With p > n the likelihood is not identified, and the reported optimum is the search ceiling rather than an estimate.

They are replaced here by a permutation null, which makes no distributional assumption: each variable’s column is permuted independently, destroying the association between variables within a scenario while preserving every variable’s marginal distribution exactly. The question it answers is the one that matters — is the observed cluster separation greater than what exchangeable data of the same shape produces?

Discussion. Two results, and they must be kept apart.

There is cluster structure, and it is unambiguous. Across 300 permutations the observed silhouette is never matched at any k from 2 to 8, in any of the three variable sets — not one of the 300 draws matched it, so the permutation p-value is below the resolution of the test, 0.0033 (0 exceedances out of 300) — with observed values 2.5 to 11.9 times the null mean. The earlier reading — that a gap statistic and a BIC of k=1 indicated no structure — was wrong: those criteria are uninformative here, not negative.

The number of clusters is still not identified. On the pooled variable set the silhouette is highest at k=2 (0.576 in the joint space) and falls from there to a local bump at k=5 (0.489) that is below the k=2 value and is not an interior maximum. That is the expected behaviour of a relative criterion at n=12, and it is what the fourteen do too: withholding the construction pair does not make the number of clusters identifiable, it makes the partition at a given k recoverable. Reported this way round deliberately, because a reader who took the exact k=4 recovery for a selected k would be reading a choice into the data that is not there.

The consequence for this analysis is methodological. Because k is not identified, the four-group taxonomy cannot be discovered from these data. It can, however, be tested: it is a partition specified in advance on mechanistic grounds, and the question is whether clustering recovers it. That question is answered with the adjusted Rand index (ARI), which counts the scenario pairs two partitions agree about, corrected for chance — 0 is chance-level agreement, 1 is identity.

5.5 Which Variables Carry the Regime Signal?

The regimes are named for transmission mechanisms — Production Leakage, Competitive Displacement, Fossil Import Collapse, Symmetric Contraction, Construction Rebound. None names an ecological outcome. If that naming is more than rhetorical, the regime signal should sit in the variables through which transmission runs, and not in the ecological satellite accounts.

That is testable. Each of the six blocks defined above is clustered on its own, in both spaces, and its partition at the taxonomy’s own k (4) scored against the taxonomy.

Discussion. The blocks differ enormously in what they carry, and the pattern is systematic.

Three blocks now recover the taxonomy exactly, in both spaces. Real activity, Finance & wealth and the pooled all-variable set each reach ARI 1.000 at k=4, in the divergence space and the joint space alike; Fiscal, External and Labour & distribution follow at 0.926; and only the Ecological block falls below that. Six of the seven blocks therefore agree with the taxonomy at 0.926 or better, and the two coordinate spaces agree with each other in every row.

The External block is still the sharpest small block, and it is right on the twelve. In the divergence space it retains only two usable variables — imp and rex, once cab and tb have cancelled — and reaches a silhouette of 0.761, the highest in the table, with ARI 0.926. Cross-border trade flows discriminate the regimes as well as real activity does, on a fraction of the variables.

The Ecological block still carries the least regime information: ARI 0.553 in the divergence space and 0.553 in the joint space, the two lowest figures in the table on this registry too. This is the substantive finding of the section, not a nuisance result, and the exclusion strengthens rather than weakens it: removing the two scenarios that dominated the distance matrix raises every other block to 0.926 and leaves this one at 0.553. Transmission regimes are constituted in the trade and real-activity structure; ecological outcomes are consequences of those regimes rather than definitions of them. The regime taxonomy and the ecological results are therefore logically independent, which is what allows the paper to report an ecological trilemma within a regime rather than confounding the two.

The previously published specification — all variables, divergence space — is now one of the best cells in the table, where on the fourteen it was the second-worst (ARI 0.565). On the twelve it reaches 1.000, equal to the joint-space figure. It pooled a strong real-activity and external signal with an ecological block that carries none, and differencing did not cost it the partition — the cost was the two scenarios the divergence space was most sensitive to.

5.6 Does the Data Recover the Four-Group Taxonomy?

Adjusted Rand index between the data partition and the taxonomy of 4 groups, by k and coordinate space, on the full variable set of 12 scenarios.
Space k=2 k=3 k=4 k=5 k=6
Divergence 0.437 0.928 1.000 0.924 0.884
Joint 0.437 0.928 1.000 0.924 0.884

On the full variable set in the joint space, the k=4 partition matches the taxonomy at ARI 1.000. In the divergence space the same cut reaches only 1.000.

That partition is stable: removing each of the 72 columns in turn and re-clustering gives an adjusted Rand index of 1.000 against the full-set partition in 72 of 72 cases. Bootstrap resampling of the variable set (500 replicates, columns drawn with replacement) gives mean ARI 0.974, with 95% of replicates at or above 0.8.

Two of the 4 regimes are recovered exactly by almost every specification. Production Leakage {Sc1, Sc4, Sc9} and Symmetric Contraction {Sc3, Sc6, Sc7, Sc8, Sc11, Sc12} — 9 of the 12 scenarios — appear with no errors in 12 of the 12 block-and-space combinations scoring at or above ARI 0.8. They are the solid core of the taxonomy.

The remaining disagreements are confined to the high-leverage scenarios and are systematic, not random. Sc10 (Mtl-Int) never forms its own cluster, attaching to {Sc2, Sc13} in the real-activity and finance blocks and elsewhere in the full joint set. Sc13 (Enrg-Int) moves too, and with the construction pair gone it is the largest divergence in the set rather than the second. These facts are reported as findings rather than smoothed away; the implications for “Competitive Displacement” as a standalone regime are taken up below.

A caution on variable selection. Drawing random subsets of the pooled divergence variables, silhouette does not land on k=4 reliably, and searching over subsets until one yields 4 clusters would therefore not be evidence. Two things distinguish the results above from that failure: the six blocks are a pre-existing economic partition of the variables rather than a search, and the reason for expecting real activity and external flows to carry the signal is stated independently of the result.

5.7 Cluster Assignments Across k

Discussion. This panel is the most direct comparison between the data-driven structure and the taxonomy, and with the construction pair withheld the comparison comes out clean:

The taxonomy appears whole at k=4. At k=4 the partition is {Sc1, Sc4, Sc9} / {Sc3, Sc6, Sc7, Sc8, Sc11, Sc12} / {Sc2, Sc13} / {Sc10} — Production Leakage, Symmetric Contraction, Fossil Import Collapse and Competitive Displacement, exactly. The same partition appears in both coordinate spaces, which is the second thing that changes: the divergence space and the joint space now agree at every k from 2 to 6, whereas on the fourteen they disagreed sharply (ARI 0.565 against 0.936 at k=5).

Stable groupings across all k: Sc3, Sc6, Sc7, Sc8, Sc11, Sc12 (Symmetric Contraction) are in one cluster at every k. Sc1, Sc4, Sc9 (Production Leakage) cohere from k=3, and it is Sc1 that leaves again at k=5 — the same scenario that did so on the fourteen, and for the same reason: Food-HH has the largest household channel, so it is the furthest of the three from the other two.

The three high-leverage scenarios separate together, then divide. Sc2, Sc10 and Sc13 hold one cluster at k=2 and k=3; at k=4 they divide into {Sc2, Sc13} and {Sc10}, which is the taxonomy’s Fossil Import Collapse / Competitive Displacement boundary; at k=6 Sc2 and Sc13 part from each other. Nothing here replicates the fourteen’s {Sc10, Sc14} pairing, because Sc14 is not in the data.

5.8 Silhouette Plots by k

Discussion. Silhouette plots reveal which specific scenarios are most and least confidently classified at each k. Average silhouette width is 0.449 at k=3, 0.462 at k=4 and 0.488 at k=5.

At k=3, the symmetric-contraction core scores 0.75–0.79 and the leakage trio 0.28–0.29, while the merged {Sc2, Sc10, Sc13} group scores 0.08–0.36. Sc9 (Plst-Int) is the only negative coefficient (−0.01): inside the leakage group it sits marginally closer to the symmetric core, which is the same near-boundary position Sc9 occupies on the fourteen.

At k=4, the cut that reproduces the taxonomy exactly, every group except {Sc10} is tight: the symmetric core 0.74–0.79, the leakage trio 0.28–0.29, and {Sc2, Sc13} at 0.21 and 0.46. Sc10 is a singleton and so scores 0 by definition. The mean rises to 0.462, from 0.449 at k=3.

At k=5, Sc1 becomes the singleton (0 by definition) and the leakage trio splits into {Sc4, Sc9} (0.66–0.74) and Sc1 alone; Sc10 stays a singleton. The mean is 0.488. Nothing at k=5 corresponds to a fifth regime — with the construction scenarios withheld, the fifth cluster is a split inside Production Leakage.

7 Discussion of Main Findings

7.1 The Exclusion, and What It Changes

This section runs the specification twice on the same long-term deviations — once on the fourteen scenarios and once on the twelve this document analyses — so that the effect of the exclusion is measured here rather than quoted from the other render. Nothing is re-tuned between the two runs: the variable blocks, the standardisation, the linkage, the distance and the reference partition are identical, and only the scenario registry differs. The reference partition is the four-group one in both runs, because that is the partition both candidate taxonomies agree on and the only one that can be used on both sides of the comparison: the paper’s fifth regime has no members once the construction pair is withheld.

The same specification on two registries. Adjusted Rand index against the four-group partition; the partition column gives the k=4 cut itself, as scenario numbers.
Registry Space p best k (silhouette) silhouette at k=4 ARI at k=4 ARI at k=5 partition at k=4
all 14 Joint 72 2 0.403 0.826 0.938 {1,4,9} {2,10,13,14} {3,6,7,8,11,12} {5}
all 14 Divergence 34 2 0.424 0.494 0.573 {1} {2,10,13,14} {3,4,6,7,8,9,11,12} {5}
these 12 Joint 72 2 0.479 1.000 0.924 {1,4,9} {2,13} {3,6,7,8,11,12} {10}
these 12 Divergence 34 2 0.462 1.000 0.924 {1,4,9} {2,13} {3,6,7,8,11,12} {10}

The exclusion makes the taxonomy recoverable, and it makes the two coordinate spaces agree. On the twelve the k=4 partition is {1,4,9} {2,13} {3,6,7,8,11,12} {10} — Production Leakage, Symmetric Contraction, Fossil Import Collapse and Competitive Displacement, exactly — and the adjusted Rand index against the four-group partition is 1.000 in both spaces. On the fourteen the same cut reaches 0.826 in the joint space and 0.494 in the divergence space, and the two spaces disagree at every k (at k=5, 0.938 joint against 0.573 divergence, both against the same four-group partition). Two consequences follow, and both are properties of the twelve rather than of the taxonomies:

  • The four regimes of the twelve are the partition the data produce at k=4, not merely a hypothesis they fail to reject. The two largest regimes are the second split of the hierarchy (see “Dendrogram” above), and the Fossil/Displacement boundary is the third.
  • The divergence space stops being the worse coordinate. Differencing still destroys the sign information in principle, but on the twelve it does not destroy the partition: the two spaces give the identical cut at every k from 2 to 6. The fourteen’s weaker divergence-space figures were therefore not evidence about the coordinate transform — that transform is the one thing the two runs share, so a difference between them cannot be its doing.

What the exclusion does not do. It does not make the number of clusters identifiable. The silhouette still peaks at k=2 on the twelve, just as it does on the fourteen, and declines from there; the taxonomy’s k is not selected by any relative criterion in either run, and the test remains a pre-specified one. Nor does the comparison distinguish the two candidate taxonomies from each other: the four- and five-regime hypotheses differ only in how they classify the construction pair, so removing that pair makes them the same partition and leaves nothing for a comparison of them to disagree about. The exclusion settles the count by removing the scenarios the count was in dispute about; it does not adjudicate between the two readings of those scenarios, which remain what the all-fourteen render reports.

7.2 What the Divergence Space Groups on the Twelve

On the fourteen, the argument of “Why the coordinate space matters” — that differencing removes the sign information the regimes are defined by — was borne out by the result: the divergence space reached ARI 0.565 where the joint space reached 0.936. On the twelve it is not borne out. Both spaces produce the identical partition at every k from 2 to 6, and the divergence space’s own k=3 cut is three of the four regimes plus a merged high-leverage group:

  • k=2: the core nine — Sc1, Sc3, Sc4, Sc6, Sc7, Sc8, Sc9, Sc11, Sc12 — against the three high-leverage scenarios Sc2, Sc10, Sc13. The split is by magnitude of transmission, not by mechanism, and it is the same in both spaces.
  • k=3: {Sc1, Sc4, Sc9} (Production Leakage) and {Sc3, Sc6, Sc7, Sc8, Sc11, Sc12} (Symmetric Contraction) separate from each other inside the core, leaving {Sc2, Sc10, Sc13} still merged.
  • k=4: {Sc2, Sc10, Sc13} divides into {Sc2, Sc13} (Fossil Import Collapse) and {Sc10} (Competitive Displacement), which is the taxonomy.

So the divergence space’s failure on the fourteen was not a property of the coordinate transform. The transform does destroy the sign information, and a pair of scenarios whose regime is defined by opposite signs (EU up against RoW down) cannot in general be separated from one whose regions move together once the sign is removed. But on these data the asymmetry profile alone separates Sc10 from Sc2 and Sc13, and the failure was caused instead by the two construction scenarios, whose divergences are large enough to dominate the distances on which the other twelve are merged.

7.3 On “Competitive Displacement” as a Standalone Regime

The original justification for isolating Sc10 (Mtl-Int) as “Competitive Displacement” rests on a mechanistic distinction: it is the only scenario in the set where EU macro variables move positive while RoW macro variables move negative simultaneously (true sign reversal). In all other high-divergence scenarios, both regions move in the same direction — EU contracts less than RoW, but both contract.

On the twelve the picture reverses, and it is worth being careful about why. Sc10 is a singleton at k=4, at k=5 and at k=6 — it never merges into the Fossil group, where on the fourteen it did. The k=4 partition is the four-group taxonomy exactly. Taken at face value that is the strongest support “Competitive Displacement” can get from this method: the cut that reproduces the other three regimes is the same cut that puts Sc10 on its own.

But it is support from a single scenario, and that is its whole strength. Sc10 cannot be corroborated from within: its ARI contribution is one cluster containing one member, and a one-member cluster is trivially “recovered” by any cut that puts it anywhere. The evidence that Sc10 is a regime rather than an unusual scenario is the mechanistic one — the sign reversal — and the reason it is now on its own is the same as the reason the fourteen’s result was weaker: with Sc5 and Sc14 out, the largest divergences in the set belong to Sc13, and the distance at which Sc10 separates from the fossil pair is small in absolute terms.

Recommendation: on this evidence, keep “Competitive Displacement” as a labelled regime only with the count stated as one, and note in the manuscript that its statistical support rests on a single scenario whose separation is by direction and not by magnitude. That is the reading the twelve support, and it is a weaker claim than the four-regime recovery of the other three regimes would suggest on its own.

7.4 Why Energy Dominates

One structural feature of the model explains the extreme salience of the energy (Sc13) scenario, which is the largest divergence in this render:

Energy (Sc13): The intermediate energy channel is simultaneously the largest channel in the scenario set (14.8 billion EUR) and the most intensity-differential material pair (emission intensity ratio 3.3:1 between secondary and primary energy). These two factors — scale and intensity differential — are multiplicative in the ΔM formula, making Sc13 the highest-leverage ecological scenario by construction. The cross-border fiscal effect is equally extreme because EU fossil fuel imports represent a direct bilateral income transfer: reducing them by ρ=0.2 removes a substantial, concentrated revenue stream from RoW hydrocarbon exporters without any compensating income source within the model’s RoW structure.

Construction (Sc5). The construction channel operates through investment, not consumption or intermediate demand, and its investment base (88.7 billion EUR, 66.7% of total construction demand) is the largest single channel in the scenario set; that, rather than the size of ρ, is why Sc5 generated the largest absolute divergences on the fourteen, including the emissions rebound of +5.14. It is withheld from this render, and the two paragraphs on the construction channel and on the validity of the “Construction Rebound” label are consequently absent: they are claims about data this render does not contain. They are carried in output/html/cross_border_analysis.html, which is where the construction scenarios are analysed.
